cover letter
Advanced degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience or training.
Academic background and experience in science communication, including writing and editing reports of research activities.
Financial and administrative experience in a university setting, with a demonstrated understanding of research environments.

Experience with project management and demonstrated leadership skills, including exceptional organizational skills sufficient to coordinate multiple ongoing projects of significant complexity, develop new programs, balance competing needs, and attend to detail.

Experience in financial planning, analysis, and budgeting sufficient to develop and manage budgets, including demonstrated quantitative skills in preparing statistical reports and budget projections, and demonstrated experience identifying and pursuing external funding opportunities.

Under the general direction of the CITRIS Director at UC Santa Cruz, the Executive Director independently oversees the operation of CITRIS programs at UC Santa Cruz and plays a key role in developing and implementing short- and long-term plans for UCSC CITRIS programs and events.

As a liaison for CITRIS, the Executive Director stewards ongoing relationships with faculty and researchers at UC Santa Cruz, other UC campuses participating in CITRIS, other educational institutions, and nonprofit and corporate members. The Executive Director also facilitates new collaborative relationships between UC Santa Cruz and partners, including nonprofit and corporate members.

The Executive Director is responsible for a variety of functions for CITRIS at UC Santa Cruz, including financial administration, budget planning, planning and organizing CITRIS-related meetings and events, developing and managing websites, coordinating infrastructure, overseeing and evaluating of CITRIS-sponsored projects, coordinating research and incubator proposal calls and submissions, and mentoring UCSC CITRIS staff.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work a hybrid work schedule and must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Advanced knowledge of administrative, budgetary, human resources, and financial principles and practices.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.

Advanced verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to compose a variety of documents at a professional level and participate in meetings in which a group’s interests and abilities are represented persuasively, accurately, tactfully, and creatively.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.

Analytical skills sufficient to assimilate information from oral and written sources, develop broad knowledge of campus policies and procedures, and interpret and apply those requirements with clarity and accuracy to individual circumstances.
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Advanced ability to think creatively and independently about concepts requiring advanced analytical skills.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, sound judgment regarding a range of complex issues, and the tact and diplomacy necessary to collaborate effectively with individuals within CITRIS, the University, and outside organizations.
Ability to cultivate professional relationships with faculty across CITRIS campuses and with staff and researchers in academic, government, and industry institutions.
Ability to work effectively with colleagues from diverse backgrounds.
